reason: The claim keeps the 5 deg fold rule only under a reading the model chose for itself. The row records fold_margin 5.0 ('margin 5'), but the model never checks th, the J1-J3 angle's distance from the J1-J2-J3 dyad's fold (tools/concept_kit.py lines 25-30, the one metric the rule names). J2 is placed by the slot law (q2 = f(q1)), the J2-J3-J4 dyad is clamped at m3 = 0.5 deg, and the 5 deg is applied to a different angle: the slaved map's singular distance (sing_deg 5). Measured with the model unchanged. Claim bench (Bench(60,160) fast, 50.67 reproduced): th margin min 0.00 deg, median 0.19; 186 of 203 taken poses (91.6 %) under 5. Frozen Bench(110,360) exact wear: min 0.00, median 0.18; 359 of 388 (92.5 %) under 5. J2 sits within 2.1 deg (p05) to 7.4 deg (median) of straight and passes through straight. Under the rule as written, the design keeps 17 of 203 taken poses (fast) and 29 of 388 (exact), so the number exists only under its own reading. The model's own reading holds: sing min 8.04 deg fast, 7.27 deg exact. The J3-dyad margin min is 0.80 deg fast and 0.97 deg exact (3 and 7 poses under 5). The same pattern is gamed on dipped-law-groove-knuckle-3r. CLAUDE.md: 'A different reading is the user's call, not the model's.'

reason: The cam may take poses at pressure angles where a roller-in-groove binds. The model accepts a pose at pa = cos(pressure angle) >= 0.25, i.e. up to 75.5 deg. Over the taken poses pa is min 0.59 (53.8 deg), p05 0.67 (47.9 deg), median 0.96 on the claim bench, and min 0.58 (54.5 deg), p05 0.66 (48.7 deg) on the frozen exact wear. So at least 5 % of taken poses drive the slaved J2 through the groove at more than 45 deg, beyond the usual 30-45 deg limit for a roller follower. In the unpowered MVP1 the arm drives J1 and the groove must push J2, so this shows up as friction or a stick the wearer feels. The bench prices none of it.
